title: Sonata
text:
Eyes that discover

        the voice of things.



        Ears that hear

        the passing of roses.



        Smell that fuses everything

        into a single aroma.



        Tongue that longs for

        the taste of another.



        Body the absence

        suffered by the four



        senses that carry it.

        Body that barely enjoys.



        It lacks touch.

        It has too much memory.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Mitre's sequence of senses and the final imbalance between missing touch and excess memory.

editorial_note: The source catalog title differs, but the body is 'Sonata'; this version preserves the visible heading.

title: It Is Better That We Met Now
text:
It is better that we met now.

If we had met earlier

we would already be separated.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Kilpi's plain, aphoristic compression.

title: Now I Wash Last Summer's Semen Off Me...
text:
Now I wash last summer's semen off me.

Little, but still

it is a pity.

Not everything suited me,

and the winter is long.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's stark bodily image and dry turn toward winter.

title: Love Is the Most Elastic Human Dimension
text:
Love is the most elastic human dimension.

It is like the vagina:

it adapts to large and small.


Nature does not disappoint.
editorial_note: The translation preserves Kilpi's frank analogy and clipped conclusion.
